newsitem.title: USA: Nearby CBOT soybeans end higher, funds buy late.
newsitem.headline: Nearby CBOT soybeans end higher, funds buy late.

text.p: Nearby soybean futures ended sharply higher Friday after commodity fund buying pushed the nearby contracts into buy-stop orders, CBOT traders said.
"It's the funds again," said one floor trader. "There was just nothing for sale at these levels, and we hit stops."

The session had been largely uneventful until Rosenthal Collins stepped in late and bought up to 3 million bushels May. Also in late trade, Refco and Iowa Grain each bought two million bushels May, floor sources said.
Traders said technical weakness had prompted much of the market's earlier weakness.
The May soybean contract's inability to break through resistance seen at $8.00 per bushel on Thursday spurred earlier fresh sales on Friday, traders said.

A slowdown in the National Oilseed Processors Assn. crush was viewed as a sign that demand for U.S. soybeans, especially for export, was waning and considered slightly bearish for futures, traders said.
NOPA put the latest week's crush at 29.970 million bushels, down from 30.864 bushels the previous week.
CBOT soybeans closed up one to 9-1/4 cents a bushel, with March up 7-3/4 at $7.91 a bushel and May up 9-1/4 at $7.93-1/4.

Friday was first notice day for the March contract and soybean deliveries come in within expectations. The CBOT reported deliveries of 1.34 million bushels. That figure fell within expectations for one to two million, traders said.
Other players included ADM buying of seven million bushels May and two million March, floor sources said, and Cargill sold one million March and E D and F Man sold 1.5 million May.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 78,000 contracts, well below the 92,933 traded Thursday.
In soybean options, Cargill Investor Services bought 400 May $8.00 calls and Term Commodities bought 300 May $8.00 calls and sold 100 July $7.75 calls.
